column1: # Words Hindi speakers routinely write in Devanagari but which are NOT
# phonetically derivable from the Hindi phonetic rules: English spelling says
# little about English sound, so "school" would come out स्चूल and "phone"
# फोने. Typed on the Hindi phonetic layout, the English spelling on the left
# resolves directly to the Hindi form on the right, ahead of the rules and of
# A hand-written draft that wants a Hindi speaker's review (issue #239). A wrong
# entry here is worse than a missing one, since it outranks everything.
# Format: english<TAB>hindi   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# Keep the English key lowercase. First column is matched case-insensitively.
# No "hi": on this layout it is ही, a word typed far more often than the greeting.
